acq_7's failure rate over the last 24 hours is 14.7% [GENIE-4528fd17]. That almost certainly breaches its SLA.

- **SLA threshold:** acq_7 is in breach when its failure rate is above 5% over a rolling 6-hour window [DOC-FEE-001 p.2].
- **Why a breach is near-certain:** The SLA is measured on 6-hour windows, and I only have the 24-hour figure. A 24-hour rate of 14.7% is the average of four consecutive 6-hour windows. At least one of those windows must therefore be at or above 14.7%, which is over 5%.
- **Supporting signal:** A recent #ops-incidents post says acq_7 is "climbing again" with many timeouts [SLACK-OPS-023 p.1].
- **If it's a breach:**
  - Meridian can claim a service credit of 10% of the month's processing fees paid to acq_7.
  - Finance must be notified within 24 hours of detection.
  - Finance files the claim within 21 days.
  - Escalation contact: acq7-escalations@example.com [DOC-FEE-001 p.2].

I haven't pulled the actual 6-hour rolling figures. I can query those if you need them to confirm the breach.

acq_7 has caused SGD 2,130.61 in refundable failed payments over the last 24 hours [GENIE-25eee836].

**Yes, a batch that size needs approval.**
- Any refund batch above SGD 500 needs approval from a member of meridian-admin before it runs [DOC-RB-021 p.1] [DOC-REF-003 p.1].
- The approver can't be the requester [DOC-RB-021 p.1].
- The approval ID must be recorded on the batch, or the refund_batch function won't run [DOC-RB-021 p.1].
- Approvals expire after 48 hours [DOC-RB-021 p.1].

An older ops note, DOC-NOTE-250 (2025-09-10), sets the threshold at SGD 250. DOC-RB-021 (2026-08-26) and DOC-REF-003 v3 (2026-08-31) are more recent, so I followed the SGD 500 threshold. SGD 2,130.61 is over both thresholds, so the answer is the same either way.

Only one acquirer is degraded right now: **acq_7**. Its recent failure rate is 16.2% on a recent volume of 5,573.51 [GENIE-cbd28df9].

**Runbook: RB-014, Acquirer degradation response (v3, modified 2026-09-25).** [DOC-RB-014 p.1] This matches the triage runbook, which routes a single degraded acquirer to RB-014 [DOC-RB-005 p.1]. A single degraded acquirer is SEV2, so acknowledge within 30 minutes [DOC-RB-005 p.1]. Ops-incidents also shows a drift check flagged acq_7 and that someone is already following RB-014 [SLACK-OPS-024 p.1].

Steps, in order [DOC-RB-014 p.1–2]:
- **Before s1:** Page PayOps on-call. That is the PagerDuty schedule `payops-primary` [SLACK-OPS-004 p.1].
- **s1:** Use `ask_genie` to get the failure rate against the 14-day baseline. Also list failed payments with refundable failure codes.
- **s2:** Retrieve the acquirer's SLA clause. The clause is Finance-restricted. If you aren't entitled to it, stop and escalate to Finance.
- **s3:** Compute customer impact. Sum the failed payments whose code is `issuer_unavailable` or `timeout`.
- **s4:** Propose a refund batch with the total in SGD.
- **s5:** Request approval from a `meridian-admin` member other than the requester. This is required if the batch is above SGD 500.
- **s6:** Execute the refund batch. It is refused unless s1–s4 are logged ok, and, above the threshold, a valid approval exists.

Only the latest approved version of the runbook may be executed [DOC-RB-014 p.2].

- **acq_7 volume:** acq_7 processed 361 payments in the last 24 hours. That window is measured back from the latest data available, not from the current time. [GENIE-5fec3db1]
- **Who to page:** Page the PayOps on-call, which is the PagerDuty schedule `payops-primary`. [SLACK-OPS-004 p.1] The runbook for a degraded acquirer also says to page PayOps on-call before starting its steps. [DOC-RB-014 p.1]
